Apple has been waiting a very long time to launch its first foldable iPhone, while Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series has already reached its eighth generation.

Apple originally had every reason to hold off, but based on Samsung's latest experience, the timing for this iPhone maker to enter the market could not be more perfect...

Apple's Long Wait

Samsung was among the earliest companies to enthusiastically embrace foldable smartphones, but quickly discovered it had moved too hastily. The first-generation Samsung Galaxy Fold had an extremely fragile display prone to damage, forcing the company to eventually pull it from sale.

Meanwhile, Apple has patiently waited for display technology to mature — not only significantly more durable, but also with virtually no visible crease when unfolded. Reports indicate Apple even had to send its own design engineers to help Samsung achieve this.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Proves the Time Is Right

We mentioned last month that the display used in Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 is strikingly similar to that of the upcoming iPhone Ultra. Our sister site 9to5Google found that the new device indeed delivers on its promise — once unfolded, the crease in the middle of the screen is barely noticeable.

But the significance goes beyond Samsung finally solving the display technology issue — consumer demand has finally caught up as well. 9to5Google reports that initial demand for the Fold 8 is triple that of its predecessor.

This figure builds on last year's already 50% growth in demand.

Of course, these two things are likely interrelated — a crease-free display dramatically boosts appeal — but factoring in last year's growth rate, it's clear that foldables have been around long enough now that more people are starting to see the benefits of this form factor.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to debut next month alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. Expectations are that this new device could quickly capture around 25% of the overall foldable smartphone market.
